topic: Drag analysis, induced, parasite, form, skin friction, profile and total drag.
syllabus_extract: Drag analysis, induced, parasite, form, skin friction, profile and total drag. D-V curve.
specific_objectives: 6.1.2.1 Trainee will be able to describe various types of aerofoil sections, conditions of performance, theories, and concept related with performance

training_aids.remarks: Refer to the master syllabus reference list
Objective: teach the syllabus extract for this lesson

practical: Activity: Drag component identification on airframe diagram. Safety: Handle diagrams carefully. Supervision: Instructor guided.
intro_questions: Define lift and its direction relative to airflow.
State Newton's Third Law in context of flight.
What is the primary force opposing forward motion?

development.content:
Parasite drag definition and components
Form drag and pressure differential
Skin friction and surface roughness

Induced drag and wingtip vortices
Angle of attack influence
Profile drag composition

Total drag calculation method
Drag vs Velocity curve analysis
Minimum drag speed identification

summary_questions: Explain how induced drag changes with speed.
Calculate total drag given parasite and induced values.
home_assignment_question: Research how high-lift devices affect induced drag for LP 14.

pft_rows.syllabus: Lift augmentation. High lift devices. Boundary Layer control
